newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Holiday mood slows movement.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Holiday mood slows movement.

text.p: Soybean meal movement was slow in U.S. rail and truck markets on Tuesday as the Christmas holiday approached and end-users waited for the CBOT December contract to expire, brokers said.

"I think the holiday mood has set in," one Tennessee broker said. "Most people have shipped what they need to ship to get it there before Christmas. They're just trying to get their hedges covered on the (CBOT) December and get out."
End-users were buying small amounts to meet immediate needs but most were waiting for the December to expire. The December was trading at an $11 premium to the January.
Brokers in several Illinois and Kansas locations began quoting offers against the January. Most carried about $6 to $8 of the Dec/Jan spread.
Cold weather across much of the United States was supportive as livestock feeders increased protein content in feed rations, but brokers said immediate soymeal needs were filled.
Export activity was said to be quiet but CIF and FOB values on the Ohio River were quoted nominally at $25 and $29 over the CBOT January.
